messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

message.content: The largest confirmed “planet” (in the sense of a sub‑stellar object orbiting a star) that astronomers have found so far is **HD 100546 b**. It has a radius roughly 2½–3 times that of Jupiter and a mass estimated at about 20 Jupiter masses. That places it right on the boundary between massive planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs, so some researchers classify it as a super‑Jovian planet while others consider it a young brown dwarf. In short, the biggest thing we’ve confidently identified as a planet is only about 20 times heavier than Jupiter—though the exact classification depends on how you draw the line between planet and brown dwarf.
